preamble: Each across clue contains a word that must be removed before solving. The first and last letters from these words, in clue order, explain changes required, to varying degrees of effect, in all down answers prior to entry. Two thematic phrases are formed of four answers.

clue.text: Parrot broke shell almost covering peeled spuds

indicators.note: covering means the shell's letters wrap around the potato letters, sitting outside them
almost means the word for shell stops short of its final letter

parts.note: a cockle is a bivalve shellfish, and so a shell

indicators.note: peeled means the potatoes lose their skins, the outer letters of the word

parts.note: taties is a Scottish and northern dialect word for potatoes, like spuds

explanation.surface: A parrot cracks open a nearly whole shell that has been wrapped round some peeled potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' is the word the preamble says to remove before solving. 'almost' trims COCKLE to COCKL, 'peeled' strips TATIES to ATIE, and 'covering' wraps the first round the second; taties is a Scottish word for potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatiel is a small crested Australian bird belonging to the cockatoo family of parrots.

clue.text: Wine winner Jonathan the cricketer losing wickets

parts.note: a champ is a champion

indicators.note: losing something means it goes, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Jonathan Agnew is an England bowler turned BBC cricket commentator
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: The champion drinks wine as cricketer Jonathan loses wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: The magnet rule lifts N two cells, so the grid shows CHAMPNAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling white made in the Champagne region of France.

clue.text: Finish ends of metal effigy in an attentive manner

parts.note: to close is to end or finish

indicators.note: the last letter of each word is used

parts.note: the two words whose last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A sculptor puts the final touches to a metal statue with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: In the grid S is pulled three cells down to the foot, so CLOELYS is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch closely is to pay careful attention to detail.

clue.text: Street artist bolstering sailor before court summary

indicators.note: to bolster is to prop up from below, so in a down answer these letters sit under the next piece
one piece comes before the next

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
St is the abbreviation for street
RA is a Royal Academician
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A graffiti artist props up a sailor ahead of a court summing-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Street artist looks like Banksy but splits into two abbreviations. S drops two cells, giving ABTRSACT in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short statement of the main points of a paper or case.

clue.text: Main outcrop has a landlord

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small island rising out of the sea, the main
second meaning, read as two words: is let, rented out by an owner

explanation.surface: A rocky outcrop at sea turns out to be rented from a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is the old poetic word for the open sea. In the grid S slips two cells down, giving ILEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a tiny island, and a property that is let is being rented to a tenant.

clue.text: Relax thin leg cryptically

definitions.meaning: the clue words are what the answer itself would produce as a cryptic clue
says to read the answer as a cryptic instruction: lighten, mixed up

explanation.surface: A command to unwind given to someone with a skinny leg.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read cryptically, the answer says jumble LIGHTEN, which gives THIN LEG. N rises two cells, so LIGHNTEUP is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is an informal phrase for becoming less serious or tense.

clue.text: Throw old man aboard craft away from the others

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be inside a vessel, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: art is skill, as in the craft of the potter
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: An old sailor is pitched overboard, far from his shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Throw is the extra word, giving T and W. Without it, the boat becomes an artistic skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart describes something set at a distance, separated from the rest of a group.

clue.text: Passionate time with Gordon's girl

parts.note: Dale Arden is Flash Gordon's companion in the comic strip and films
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A torrid spell spent with the hero's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: In the grid N moves three cells up, giving ANRDET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning with feeling, an eager and fervent synonym for passionate.

clue.text: Expiratory sound at 13.00? Get away

parts.note: taken as written
1 pm is one o'clock on the 24-hour clock, so the number one, as the Roman I
shoo is what you say to drive off an animal

explanation.surface: A sigh heard at one in the afternoon, followed by a cry of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: S slips one cell down in the grid, giving ATIHSOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the British spelling of a sneeze's sound, a sudden explosive breath out.

clue.text: Article outlines another one of Alfred's nobles?

indicators.note: to outline something is to draw round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: the is the definite article
a second article, the indefinite one

explanation.surface: A history piece sketches yet another of King Alfred's lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Another means a second article after the first. N moves two cells up, giving TNHAE in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane held land from an Anglo-Saxon king, such as Alfred the Great, in return for service.

clue.text: One of twelve in spinning exercise felt so paranoid

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run of words the answer hides in, read backwards

explanation.surface: One juror, dizzy after a workout, feels the others are plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: Exercise is the extra word, giving E and E. The answer runs backwards through fELT SO PAranoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus chose twelve apostles, so each apostle is one member of that group of disciples.

clue.text: Butcher rang his nice bit on the side

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack up and mangle, so the letters are cut up and reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher phones his pleasant mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the extra word, giving N and E. Bit on the side looks like a lover, but here it is a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a small decorative extra served at the edge of a plate of food.

clue.text: Nationalist supports citizens of Europe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: posts or upright props that hold something up

explanation.surface: A patriot backs fellow Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: Nationalist is the extra word, giving N and T. POLES then pairs with APART for the thematic phrase POLES APART.
explanation.definitionFit: Poles are both upright wooden props and natives of Poland, a central European country.

clue.text: 10 angels regularly call on Rabbi Williams?

parts.note: the number written as a word

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one

parts.note: the word whose even-placed letters are taken
to see someone is to visit, or call on, them

explanation.surface: Ten angels take turns visiting a rabbi called Williams.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbi is the extra word, giving R and I. The question mark marks Williams as a sample of the answer: the playwright Tennessee Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams wrote A Streetcar Named Desire, so the first name defines him by example.

clue.text: Engineers link rugged seacoast and island

indicators.note: rugged means rough and broken up, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
I is the abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: Engineers join a rocky coastline to an offshore island.
explanation.walkthrough: Engineers is the extra word, giving E and S. Without it the verb link stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate two things is to connect them in the mind or in fact.

clue.text: Command concerning rear of hit vessel

parts.note: about means on the subject of

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word, its back end

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
an urn is a vase-shaped container

explanation.surface: An order is given about the stern of a ship that has been struck.
explanation.walkthrough: N climbs five cells in the grid, giving ABONUTTUR.
explanation.definitionFit: About turn is the drill-sergeant's order to face the opposite way.

clue.text: Equine tense on baleful pass

indicators.note: one piece is placed on, after, the other in the across answer

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountains
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous horse on a menacing mountain route.
explanation.walkthrough: Baleful is the extra word, giving B and L. Equine works as a noun here: a member of the horse family.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, one particular kind of horse-family animal.

clue.text: Docker outside of Dieppe checks up on mineral

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next
in a down answer up means written from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
the outside of the word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the French port whose first and last letters are kept
to vet is to check
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A port worker outside Dieppe checks up on a mineral cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: S slips two cells down, giving TESVEDORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at a port, the job of a dockworker.

clue.text: Cliff gives shelter for one with German weapon

indicators.note: to shelter something is to take it inside, so the word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff, a word common in northern England
I is the Roman numeral one
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A cliff face shelters a lone man with a German gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff wants to be Cliff Richard, but it is a rock face. S drops one cell, giving CSIMITAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved sword from the Middle East, a cutting weapon.

clue.text: Elders initially go on about Orphic songs of heroism

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to add is to go on, as in a speaker adding a remark

explanation.surface: Village elders sing on about mystical heroic ballads.
explanation.walkthrough: Orphic is the extra word, giving O and C. Go on, as in 'he went on', is a way to say add.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is the Old Norse collection of poems about gods and heroic warriors.

clue.text: Shown cleared score sheets?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as de-noted: sheets of music with their notes removed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up second sense. N rises one cell, giving DNEOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to indicate or signify, and de- can mean removing, as in de-icing.

clue.text: Fat and thin kids maybe work by river locations

parts.note: an op is a work, as in opus
the Po is Italy's longest river
sites are places where things are located

explanation.surface: Plump and skinny children labour at riverside spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Kids is the extra word, giving K and S; maybe marks fat and thin as one example. OPPOSITES joins ATTRACT for the phrase OPPOSITES ATTRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat and thin are antonyms, a pair of words with contrary meanings, as are hot and cold.

clue.text: East Asian container inscribed with letter

indicators.note: something inscribed with a word carries it written inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a tin is a container
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller's box is engraved with a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: N rises five cells to sit second in the grid, giving TNIBETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan is a native of Tibet, a Himalayan region of China.

clue.text: Women in function with guys oddly like The Shadows?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tan is the tangent function in trigonometry
W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third

parts.note: the word whose odd-placed letters are taken

explanation.surface: Women at a party with blokes act a bit like a 1960s band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shadows were Cliff Richard's guitar band, famous for a twanging electric sound. N rises three cells, giving NTWAGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Twangy describes the resonant plucked guitar tone the band was known for.

clue.text: Something animalistic barked in forest

definitions.meaning: reads as a dog yapping, but barked means covered in bark; animalistic is the extra word
places the thing among the trees, where trunks stand

explanation.walkthrough: Animalistic is the extra word, giving A and C; it was only there to sell the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree's woody main stem is clad in bark, and woods are full of them.

clue.text: Energy Nick finally increased 20-fold

indicators.note: the final letter, read as a Roman numeral, is multiplied by twenty to give a different numeral

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A man called Nick has finally boosted his energy twentyfold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally increased 20-fold' takes the last letter of STEAL, L or Roman 50, and multiplies it by twenty to make 1000, Roman M. 'Nick' looks like a name but is the verb meaning to pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is power or vigour, as in running out of steam, so it stands for energy.

clue.text: Lout climbing atop vacant snack stall

indicators.note: sitting on top, so in a down answer this piece comes first
in a down answer climbing means going upward, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an oik is a British slang word for a loutish person

indicators.note: emptied of its inside letters, leaving only the outer ones

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A yob clambers on top of an empty food stand.
explanation.walkthrough: S drops one cell, giving KIOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk is a small booth selling newspapers or snacks.

clue.text: Variety of grass tea Warren picked up

indicators.note: heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a warren is a maze of tunnels or narrow streets

explanation.surface: A man named Warren notices a kind of grass in his tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea is the extra word, giving T and A; Warren looks like a name but is a labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or corn, is a cereal crop, and cereals are members of the grass family.

clue.text: Draw edges of stadium against area of land

indicators.note: only the first and last letters, the word's edges, are kept

parts.note: the word whose two end letters are kept
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: A tie at the stadium in a match against a local side.
explanation.walkthrough: Stadium is the extra word, giving S and M; with it gone, edges of applies to against.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to pull something toward you, as a magnet pulls iron.

clue.text: 100 cycling with ageing male turn very active

indicators.note: cycling sends a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a ton is a hundred
he is the male pronoun
a go is a turn, as in it's your go

explanation.surface: A centenarian cyclist with an old man suddenly becomes a ball of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ageing is the extra word, giving A and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is busy and constantly moving, never pausing to rest.

clue.text: Confuse naive pal Mark standing in for bishop

indicators.note: a stand-in replaces someone, so one letter takes another's place

parts.note: a buddy is a friend
B is the chess notation for bishop
M is the abbreviation for the mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A trusting friend named Mark covers for the bishop, muddling everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Naive is the extra word, giving N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddy an issue is to make it less clear, clouding understanding.

clue.text: Busy RAF rescue teams appear again

indicators.note: busy letters are bustling about, so they rearrange themselves

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Hard-working air force rescue crews turn up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Teams is the extra word, giving T and S. Together the extra words read BETWEEN ENTRIES BLOCKS ACT AS MAGNETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurface is to come back up to view after being submerged or absent.
